name: flowpact
description: Data-flow linter for GitHub Actions: finds the inputs, secrets, env vars and matrix values that arrive empty while the run stays green, across reusable workflows, composite actions and matrix combinations.
description_good_justification: The README and the docs home page say in plain words what flowpact does: it is a data-flow linter for GitHub Actions that finds inputs, secrets, env vars and matrix values that end up empty while the run still passes, across reusable workflows, local actions and matrix combinations. See https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact#readme and https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/.
interact_justification: The README explains how to get flowpact (npm, the GitHub Action, the VS Code extension; also https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/installation), and its 'Feedback and contributing' section (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact#feedback-and-contributing) points to GitHub Issues for bugs and feature requests, SECURITY.md for vulnerabilities and CONTRIBUTING.md for contributions.
contribution_justification: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests explains the process: changes reach main through pull requests, which are squash-merged after the 'CI passed' and 'Conventional PR title' checks pass and a code owner approves. Bugs and feature requests use GitHub Issues.
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md sets the requirements: PR titles follow Conventional Commits; contributions must pass CI, which runs Biome lint, typecheck, tests on Node 22 and 24 with coverage thresholds, and fallow code health; contributors must regenerate the docs and the committed action bundle when they change.
floss_license_justification: flowpact is released under the MIT license, which is OSI-approved and FSF-free. Its bundled workflow model, ciatlas/core, is also MIT.
floss_license_osi_justification: The only license is MIT, which the OSI has approved.
license_location_justification: The license is a top-level LICENSE file in the repository: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/LICENSE.
documentation_basics_justification: The docs at https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact cover installing (npm, mise, the GitHub Action, the VS Code extension; https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/installation), a first run and reading the output (https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/getting-started), and CI setup. https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/security covers safe use: what flowpact reads, writes and sends, the permissions it needs, and that plugins run code (use --no-plugins on untrusted code).
documentation_interface_justification: Reference docs cover every external interface. The CLI's commands, options, output formats, exit codes and environment variables are at https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/cli. The Action's inputs and outputs are at https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/action. The programmatic API is at https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/api. The config file is documented at https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/configuration with published JSON Schemas, and each rule has a generated page.
sites_https_justification: Every project site uses HTTPS: the repository (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact), the docs on GitHub Pages with HTTPS enforced (https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact), and the download locations (npm, GitHub Releases, VS Code Marketplace, Open VSX). Plain HTTP requests redirect to HTTPS.
discussion_justification: Discussion happens in GitHub Issues and pull requests at https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact. They are public, searchable and URL-addressable, anyone with a GitHub account can join, and they need only a web browser.
english_justification: All documentation, the README, CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY and the code comments are in English, and the project accepts bug reports and comments in English.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained. The most recent release, 0.12.2, came out on 2026-10-12, and there have been 22 releases since 0.1.0 on 2026-10-08. SECURITY.md promises to acknowledge vulnerability reports within 3 working days.
repo_public_justification: The source is in a public Git repository at https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact.
repo_track_justification: The repository uses Git, which records what changed, who changed it and when. Every change to main also arrives as a pull request that records its author, reviewers and checks.
repo_interim_justification: Every change lands on main as its own squash-merged pull request, so the repository holds every interim version, not just releases. For example, pull requests #97 to #108 were merged between v0.12.1 and v0.12.2.
repo_distributed_justification: The project uses Git, hosted on GitHub.
version_unique_justification: Every release has its own version number (vX.Y.Z), and the npm package, the VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX use the same numbers. npm never accepts a version number twice, and since 0.10.0 every GitHub release is immutable, so its tag and files cannot change.
version_semver_justification: Releases use Semantic Versioning, as stated at the top of https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md. release-please computes each version from Conventional Commit titles: fix means patch, feat means minor, and breaking means major, also before 1.0.
version_tags_justification: Each release has a Git tag vX.Y.Z; from 0.1.1 on, the release automation creates them. A ruleset lets only the release bot and repository admins create, move or delete v* tags.
release_notes_justification: Every release has human-readable notes in https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md and on https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/releases. They are grouped into breaking changes (with upgrade steps), features, bug fixes and performance, and come from user-facing PR titles, not a raw git log. There is also an upgrade guide at https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/upgrading.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability with a CVE or similar ID has ever affected flowpact, so there is nothing for the release notes to list. Future fixes would be published as GitHub security advisories and named in the release notes.
report_process_justification: Bugs and feature requests go to GitHub Issues (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/issues), with a bug report form asking for the version, a minimal reproduction and how flowpact was run; the README's 'Feedback and contributing' section says so. Vulnerabilities are reported privately as https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/SECURITY.md describes.
report_tracker_justification: flowpact tracks bugs, enhancement requests and questions in GitHub Issues, labelled bug, enhancement and question: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/issues.
report_responses_justification: Every bug report filed so far was fixed and closed within a day: #38 by #58, and #41/#42 (duplicates) by #50. No reports yet fall in the 2-12 month window because the project only went public in October 2026, and so far all bug reports were filed by the maintainer.
enhancement_responses_justification: The only enhancement request so far, #43 (docs links in --help), was implemented the day it was filed in #50. The question #40 about whether unused outputs deserve a warning was answered by the change in #56. Both were filed by the maintainer, since the project only went public in October 2026.
report_archive_justification: All issues and pull requests, open and closed, are public and searchable along with their discussions at https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/issues and https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/pulls.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The security policy at https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/SECURITY.md (also at https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/security/policy and linked from https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/security) explains how to report a vulnerability privately, what to include, the response times and what is in scope.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Vulnerabilities are reported privately over HTTPS through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting form (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/security/advisories/new), which is enabled for the repository. https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/SECURITY.md asks reporters to use it and not public issues.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received: the repository has no security advisories in any state. SECURITY.md promises an acknowledgement within 3 working days and an assessment within 10.
build_justification: After `pnpm install`, `pnpm build` rebuilds the CLI, the GitHub Action bundle, the language server and the VS Code extension from source, as documented in CONTRIBUTING.md. CI rebuilds on every pull request and fails if the committed action bundle differs from a fresh build.
build_common_tools_justification: The build uses the standard Node.js/TypeScript toolchain: pnpm scripts, the TypeScript compiler (tsc) for type checking, and tsup (esbuild) for bundling.
build_floss_tools_justification: Building needs only FLOSS tools: Node.js and pnpm (MIT), TypeScript (Apache-2.0), and tsup and esbuild (MIT). The extension is packaged with @vscode/vsce (MIT).
test_justification: The repository includes a Vitest suite (MIT): 866 unit, property and end-to-end tests in 47 files under packages/*/test and scripts/test. CONTRIBUTING.md documents `pnpm test` and `pnpm coverage` (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), and CI runs the suite on Node 22 and 24.
test_invocation_justification: The tests run with `pnpm test`, the package.json `test` script (Vitest), which is the standard way to run tests in a Node.js project.
test_most_justification: On main, the suite covers 84% of lines, 83% of statements, 80% of functions and 73% of branches of flowpact's packages. CI fails if line coverage drops below 80% overall or 90% for packages/lint. End-to-end tests also run the packed CLI on Linux, macOS and Windows, and the extension in VS Code.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs lint, type checking, the build and the test suite on every pull request and every push to main (.github/workflows/ci.yml). The main branch ruleset requires the 'CI passed' check before a merge.
test_policy_justification: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests: a pull request that adds or changes behaviour adds tests for it, and a bug fix adds a test that fails without the fix. The required 'CI passed' check also fails when line coverage drops below 80% overall or 90% in packages/lint.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent major features shipped with tests. Examples: the programmatic API in 0.10.0 (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/pull/78, +669 lines in packages/cli/test/api.test.ts), its format functions in 0.11.0 (#84), the action's base-config and plugin inputs (#76), the language server (#35) and the VS Code extension with its end-to-end smoke test (#39).
tests_documented_added_justification: The contribution instructions say it: a pull request that adds or changes behaviour adds tests for it, next to the code they test, and a bug fix adds a test that fails without the fix (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests).
warnings_justification: TypeScript runs in strict mode (tsconfig.base.json) and the Biome linter (`pnpm lint`) checks the code. CI runs both on every pull request, together with CodeQL (extended query suite) and fallow (dead code, duplication, architecture).
warnings_fixed_justification: Type checking passes with no errors and CodeQL has no open alerts. Biome reports only 2 warnings and 1 hint across 203 files on main, all minor style findings (`!important` in the docs CSS and a property-access style in one test).
warnings_strict_justification: TypeScript goes beyond `strict` (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, noImplicitOverride, verbatimModuleSyntax, isolatedModules), and Biome's recommended rules are on with only three turned off. CodeQL uses the extended query suite, and fallow fails a pull request that adds dead code or duplication compared with main.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer (rumankazi) knows the secure design principles and applies them in flowpact. Examples: a limited attack surface (no network access or telemetry in the CLI, language server or extension), least privilege (the action needs only `contents: read`), fail-safe defaults (plugins are skipped on pull_request_target and workflow_run and load in VS Code only in trusted workspaces), and allowlist validation of config and contracts with strict schemas. See https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/security.
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common vulnerabilities for a tool that reads untrusted repository files and runs in CI, and flowpact mitigates each one. It never writes through symlinks (path traversal), escapes control characters and workflow commands in its output (output injection), reads flag values only as values (argument injection), caps YAML alias and matrix expansion (resource exhaustion), and skips plugins on untrusted triggers (code execution). See https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/security#what-it-reads-and-writes.
crypto_published_justification: flowpact implements no cryptography of its own and relies only on published, expert-reviewed algorithms: TLS (through Node.js for the GitHub Action's optional artifact upload, and through git for its optional impact-mode fetch), SHA-256 for the uploaded artifact's digest (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/packages/action/src/upload.ts), and SHA-1 only to derive non-security finding IDs. The CLI, language server and extension make no network requests (https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/security/).
crypto_call_justification: flowpact calls Node.js's built-in node:crypto (OpenSSL) for hashing and UUIDs. Its HTTPS requests go through @actions/http-client over Node's TLS, and the Action's optional impact-mode fetch runs git. It re-implements nothing cryptographic.
crypto_floss_justification: All cryptographic functionality comes from Node.js and its bundled OpenSSL, both FLOSS.
crypto_keylength_justification: flowpact generates, stores and selects no keys. Its only key exchanges are the TLS handshakes of the GitHub Action's optional network requests (the artifact upload through Node.js, the impact-mode fetch through git), which use those tools' default settings; flowpact does not change them.
crypto_working_justification: flowpact uses no broken algorithms (no MD4, MD5, DES, RC4 or Dual_EC_DRBG). Its only hashes are SHA-256, for the digest of the artifact the GitHub Action uploads, and SHA-1, for non-security finding IDs, and it leaves TLS to the default configuration of Node.js and git.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No security mechanism depends on SHA-1 or another weak algorithm, and the artifact integrity digest is SHA-256. SHA-1 is used only to derive 16-character finding IDs (SARIF partialFingerprints and editor diagnostic data), which nothing relies on for integrity or authentication (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/packages/lint/src/analyze.ts).
crypto_pfs_justification: flowpact implements no key agreement protocol. Its only encrypted connections are the GitHub Action's optional HTTPS requests, made through Node.js's TLS stack (artifact upload) and git (impact-mode fetch).
crypto_password_storage_justification: flowpact is a linter with no user accounts or inbound authentication, so it stores no passwords.
crypto_random_justification: flowpact generates no cryptographic keys. The one security-relevant random value in the shipped Action, the output-file delimiter nonce in the bundled @actions/core, comes from Node's CSPRNG (crypto.randomUUID). flowpact's own code uses Math.random only to jitter retry delays.
delivery_mitm_justification: Every channel is HTTPS: npm (with npm provenance), GitHub (the Action and the release assets, signed with Sigstore; releases are immutable since 0.10.0), the VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX. The docs site redirects HTTP to HTTPS. See https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/security/ for how to verify each artifact.
delivery_unsigned_justification: The project publishes no checksum files to be fetched over HTTP. Verification relies on signature-checked Sigstore attestations (`gh attestation verify`, `gh release verify`, `npm audit signatures`), and the release workflow passes SHA-256 values between its own jobs as job outputs, never over HTTP.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: There are no unpatched publicly known vulnerabilities in flowpact or its shipped dependencies. The repository has no security advisories, and `pnpm audit --prod` reports no known vulnerabilities in the production dependency tree.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging reports within 3 working days and assessing them within 10, with fixes released as soon as they are ready (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/SECURITY.md). In practice, high-severity CodeQL findings were fixed within a day; one, in the bundled @actions/core, was dismissed as not exploitable.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Secret scanning with push protection is enabled and has no alerts, and a search of the tree and the full git history found no private keys or tokens. Publishing to npm, the VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX uses OIDC, so no long-lived publishing token is stored.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL, with the security-extended suite for JavaScript/TypeScript and GitHub Actions, analyzes every pull request and every push to main, including the release-please release PRs (for example #109 for 0.12.2). Biome's linter runs in the required 'CI passed' check (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml).
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL runs its security-extended query suite, which targets common JavaScript/TypeScript and Actions vulnerabilities such as injection, ReDoS, insecure temporary files and untrusted checkouts.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Every confirmed medium-or-higher CodeQL finding was fixed within hours to 3 days. The rest were dismissed as false positives, test fixtures, or a race in the bundled @actions/core that is not exploitable. No medium-or-higher CodeQL alert is open.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on every pull request, on every push to main and weekly, and Biome runs in CI on every pull request and push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: A fast-check property-based fuzz test feeds the analyzer 300 random, often invalid, workflow-shaped repositories and requires that it never throws (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/packages/lint/test/robustness.test.ts). It runs in the required CI tests on every pull request, including release PRs.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: flowpact is written entirely in TypeScript and runs on Node.js, a memory-safe environment, and ships no C, C++ or other native code.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: The tests run flowpact's TypeScript sources and assert heavily: the JSON report of every fixture repository and the CLI's JSON output are validated against flowpact's report schema, and the fuzz test checks invariants on every finding (positive line and column, https docs URL).
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The fuzz test has not surfaced any medium-or-higher vulnerability: the repository has no security advisories. The test runs in the required 'CI passed' check, which has no bypass actors, so a failing case blocks merging until it is fixed.
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The ciatlas GitHub organization that owns the authoritative repository (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact) requires two-factor authentication for every member and outside collaborator, and GitHub accepts passkeys for it. The only person with access is the maintainer, as org owner and repository admin.
osps_ac_02_01_justification: Organization members get only the base permission Read on ciatlas repositories, which on this public repository grants nothing beyond what anyone already has. Outside collaborators get no access until an owner invites them with a role chosen by hand. Today the maintainer is the only member and collaborator.
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The active 'main' ruleset (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/rulesets/main.json, also shown at https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/rules) requires every change to main to arrive as a squash-merged pull request that passes the 'CI passed' and 'Conventional PR title' checks. It blocks force pushes and has no bypass actors, so not even an admin can push to main directly.
osps_ac_03_02_justification: The same 'main' ruleset includes a deletion rule and has no bypass actors (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/rulesets/main.json), so GitHub refuses to delete main for everyone. An admin would first have to take the separate, explicit step of editing or disabling the ruleset, and the weekly settings sync would revert that.
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow puts an expression directly into a shell script. Untrusted metadata such as the PR title, head ref and base ref reaches run steps only through environment variables used quoted, and the PR title is checked against a strict Conventional Commits regex (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/workflows/pr-title.yml). CodeQL's Actions queries (security-extended) and flowpact's own lint scan every workflow on each PR.
osps_br_01_03_justification: Workflows that run code from pull requests use the pull_request trigger, never pull_request_target or workflow_run. Fork PRs therefore get a read-only GITHUB_TOKEN and no secrets, and a first-time contributor's run needs maintainer approval. Credentials are used only in jobs that run from main (release.yml, the 'Apply settings' job in repo-settings.yml), and https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-bundle.yml builds Renovate's branch in a job with no secrets, giving the bot token only to a separate job that runs none of the branch's code.
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official channel is HTTPS-only. That covers the repository, issues and security advisories on https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact and the docs on GitHub Pages at https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact, where HTTPS is enforced, along with the npm, VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX pages. Plain-HTTP requests to each of them redirect to HTTPS.
osps_br_03_02_justification: Every distribution channel is authenticated. npm is served over HTTPS, with trusted publishing and npm provenance. GitHub Releases are served over HTTPS and, from 0.10.0, are immutable and covered by GitHub's signed release attestation; the npm tarball, the Action archive and the .vsix each carry a Sigstore bundle and in-toto provenance. The Action is fetched through git tags over HTTPS, which only the release bot and admins can create. The VS Code Marketplace and Open VSX are served over HTTPS. https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/security/#verify-a-release shows how to verify each artifact.
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning with push protection is on for the repository. It is kept in code at https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/security.json and re-applied weekly, so a push containing a recognized credential is rejected before it lands. Publishing uses OIDC trusted publishing and GitHub secrets, so no credential files are part of the workflow.
osps_do_01_01_justification: The docs at https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact cover installing (https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/installation/) and a first run (https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/getting-started/), the CLI (https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/cli/), the GitHub Action (https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/action/), the editors (https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/editors/), CI setup and configuration. The one dangerous capability, plugins that run repository code, is flagged with highlighted warning callouts on the Action and configuration pages and in https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/security/#plugins-run-code.
osps_do_02_01_justification: The README's 'Feedback and contributing' section (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact#feedback-and-contributing) sends bug reports to GitHub Issues, where a bug report form (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml) asks for what happened, a minimal reproduction, the flowpact version and how it was run. The CLI docs ask users to report internal errors with --debug output (https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/cli/), and vulnerabilities go privately through SECURITY.md.
osps_gv_02_01_justification: Proposed changes and usage problems are discussed publicly in GitHub Issues (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/issues) and pull requests (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/pulls). Anyone with a GitHub account can open or comment on them, and the README points users there.
osps_gv_03_01_justification: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: setup, repository layout, and pull requests that are squash-merged after the 'CI passed' and 'Conventional PR title' checks pass and a code owner approves. It also covers the test expectations, the commit message convention and how releases happen. The README links to it.
osps_le_02_01_justification: The source code is under the MIT license (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/LICENSE), which is OSI-approved and FSF-free. Its workflow model dependency, ciatlas/core, is also MIT.
osps_le_02_02_justification: Every released asset is MIT-licensed and ships the license. The npm tarball and the action archive contain LICENSE, the .vsix declares MIT and lists LICENSE among its files, and the code they bundle is under MIT, ISC, BSD-3-Clause or BlueOak-1.0.0, all OSI-approved. Each asset lists its bundled packages and their license texts in THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt and in a CycloneDX SBOM attached to the release (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/releases/tag/v0.12.2).
osps_le_03_01_justification: The MIT license is in a top-level LICENSE file at https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/LICENSE. The project's other repository, the workflow model ciatlas/core, has its own MIT LICENSE at https://github.com/ciatlas/core/blob/main/LICENSE.
osps_le_03_02_justification: Every released asset carries the license. The npm package `flowpact` includes LICENSE (packages/cli/package.json `files`), the VS Code extension .vsix includes LICENSE.txt, and the GitHub Action archive flowpact-action-X.Y.Z.tar.gz includes LICENSE next to action.yml; see https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/releases. The Action at a release tag and GitHub's source archives contain the repository's LICENSE.
osps_qa_01_01_justification: The source is in a public GitHub repository at the stable URL https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact, with no mirrors. It moved there from the maintainer's personal account in 0.12.0, and GitHub redirects the old URL.
osps_qa_01_02_justification: The public Git history at https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/commits/main records every change with its author and date. Each change arrives as a squash-merged pull request whose author is the commit author and whose individual commits stay visible on the PR. The main ruleset blocks force pushes and branch deletion for everyone, so history cannot be rewritten (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/rulesets/main.json).
osps_qa_02_01_justification: Direct dependencies are declared in the package.json of each workspace package (for example https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/packages/lint/package.json) and locked in https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/pnpm-lock.yaml. The lockfile also pins the git dependency @ciatlas/core to a commit. Each release also ships a CycloneDX SBOM of what is bundled.
osps_qa_04_01_justification: The project has two repositories. The 'The workflow model: @ciatlas/core' section of https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-workflow-model-ciatlascore documents the second one, https://github.com/ciatlas/core: what it is (the model flowpact's checks are built on), that it has its own tests and releases, and that the CLI, Action and extension bundle it from a release tag. The repository layout table in the same file lists the monorepo's own packages.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: The repository commits one generated file, the GitHub Action's bundle packages/action/dist/index.js, because GitHub runs a JavaScript action from the ref that uses: names. A required CI job rebuilds it from source on every pull request and fails on any difference (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml, job action-dist), and the release archive is built reproducibly; it remains a generated artifact in version control.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: The only binary files in the repository are PNG images: brand assets, docs screenshots and the extension icon. This control explicitly allows those. No executables, libraries, archives or other compiled binaries are committed, and the GitHub Action bundle is plain-text JavaScript that CI checks against a fresh build (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml).
osps_vm_02_01_justification: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability says how to reach the project about security issues: privately through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/security/advisories/new), which is enabled and goes to the maintainers. The README and https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/security link to it. ciatlas/core has its own SECURITY.md with the same channel.
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The GITHUB_TOKEN default is read-only, the lowest setting, for both the ciatlas organization and the repository, and workflows cannot approve pull requests, so a job that sets no permissions gets read access only. Every workflow also sets its own top-level permissions: contents: read in most, {} in pr-title.yml, read-all in scorecard.yml, and in docs.yml contents: read with pages: write and id-token: write for the Pages deployment. Other write scopes are granted only on the jobs that use them (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/tree/main/.github/workflows).
osps_br_02_01_justification: Every release gets a unique Semantic Versioning number and a vX.Y.Z tag, which release-please computes from Conventional Commit titles (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/release-please-config.json, https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). npm never accepts a version twice, releases are immutable since 0.10.0, and a ruleset lets only the release bot and admins create, move or delete v* tags.
osps_br_04_01_justification: Every release has a descriptive changelog, both on its GitHub release page (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/releases) and in https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md. It groups changes into breaking changes with upgrade steps, features, bug fixes and performance, written from user-facing PR titles. Security-relevant changes are listed too, for example 0.9.0's 'harden 0.9.0 before its release: flag values, plugins, report paths and release assets' and 0.12.1's bounded walking of linked directories.
osps_br_05_01_justification: The build and release pipelines take dependencies through pnpm, the project's standard package manager. The version is pinned in package.json's packageManager, and every CI and release job runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` against the committed lockfile (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml, https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml). Workflow actions are pinned to commit SHAs and updated by Renovate.
osps_br_06_01_justification: The npm tarball, the Action archive and the .vsix each have a Sigstore-signed SLSA build provenance attestation from GitHub Actions, attached as .sigstore.json and .intoto.jsonl, and each CycloneDX SBOM is attested against its artifact. Since 0.10.0 every release is also an immutable GitHub release whose signed release attestation lists the SHA-256 of every attached file (`gh release verify`), and the npm package has npm provenance. See https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases and https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/security/#verify-a-release.
osps_do_06_01_justification: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#dependencies describes how dependencies are selected (reviewed in a pull request, bundled into every artifact), obtained (pnpm with a frozen lockfile, a two-day minimum release age, install scripts only for allowlisted packages, @ciatlas/core from a release tag, actions pinned to commit SHAs) and tracked (Renovate, OSV vulnerability alerts, and an SBOM and license notices in every release).
osps_do_07_01_justification: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#setup lists what a build needs: Node.js 22 or later, and pnpm, pinned in package.json and enabled with `corepack enable`. It also gives the commands. `pnpm install` fetches every dependency from the lockfile, including the workflow model @ciatlas/core from its GitHub release tag (explained in the next section). `pnpm build` bundles the CLI and the GitHub Action.
osps_gv_01_01_justification: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#access-to-sensitive-resources lists everyone and everything with access to the project's sensitive resources: the GitHub organization and repositories, the two GitHub Apps and their permissions, the release bot's credentials, and the npm, VS Code Marketplace, Azure and Open VSX accounts that publish releases.
osps_gv_01_02_justification: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#roles-and-responsibilities describes the roles (maintainer, contributors, the release bot, Renovate) and what each is responsible for, and how access is given and taken away when people join or leave.
osps_gv_03_02_justification: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests sets the requirements for an acceptable contribution. They are a Conventional Commits PR title and the required CI checks: Biome lint, typecheck, tests on Node 22 and 24, line coverage of at least 80% overall and 90% in packages/lint, and fallow code health. A behaviour change needs tests, and a bug fix needs a test that fails without it. Docs and the committed action bundle must be regenerated, and a code owner must approve.
osps_le_01_01_justification: Every change reaches main through a pull request on GitHub (the main ruleset requires one and has no bypass, https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/rulesets/main.json). Under section D.6 of GitHub's Terms of Service, contributors to this MIT-licensed repository assert they have the right to license their contributions, as https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests also states.
osps_qa_03_01_justification: The live `main` ruleset has no bypass actors and requires the 'CI passed' and 'Conventional PR title' checks to pass on an up-to-date branch before any merge (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/rulesets/main.json). 'CI passed' fails unless every CI job succeeds (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml). Renovate merges only when all checks are green. The other checks (CodeQL, code-scanning results) are informational, so merging past a failure in one of them is a manual action by the maintainer.
osps_qa_06_01_justification: On every pull request, CI's Test job runs the Vitest suite of unit, property and end-to-end tests (`pnpm coverage`) on Node 22 and 24 (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml). CI also smoke-tests the packed CLI on Linux, macOS and Windows and the extension in VS Code. The `main` ruleset requires the aggregate 'CI passed' check and has no bypass actors, so nothing merges without these tests.
osps_sa_01_01_justification: https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/how-it-works describes the analysis step by step, from YAML to reports. https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#repository-layout names each component: the core model, lint, reporters, CLI/API, action, language server and extension. https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/security covers every actor and action around them: the analyzed repository as untrusted input, plugins, what flowpact writes, the Action's two network calls and its token, and permissions. The release workflow, release bot and Renovate are covered there and in https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#releases.
osps_sa_02_01_justification: Reference docs cover every external interface of the released assets. The CLI's commands, options, output formats, JSON report, exit codes and environment variables: https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/cli. The Action's inputs, outputs, annotations and permissions: https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/action. The programmatic API: https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/api. The config, with JSON Schemas: https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/configuration. Contracts: https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/contracts. The plugin API: https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/custom-rules. The language server and extension settings: https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/editors.
osps_sa_03_01_justification: The threat model at https://ciatlas.github.io/flowpact/docs/threat-model ranks the most likely and impactful security problems by residual risk, each with the mitigation in the code, the tests that cover it and the risk that remains; CONTRIBUTING.md asks to revisit it for new features and breaking changes.
osps_vm_01_01_justification: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/SECURITY.md is the coordinated disclosure policy, also shown at https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/security/policy. Reports go privately through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting, with an acknowledgement within 3 working days and an assessment within 10. The advisory is published once a fixed release is available, crediting the reporter.
osps_vm_03_01_justification: https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability directs reporters to GitHub's private vulnerability reporting form (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/security/advisories/new) and not to public issues. The form is enabled for the repository, and reports reach the maintainer privately.
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities fixed in past releases are published in https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-fixes-in-past-releases with the affected versions, how to tell whether you are affected and the fix; future ones are published as GitHub security advisories (https://github.com/ciatlas/flowpact/security/advisories) and named in the release notes.
